annotations.title: FlightPowers: compare hotel rates across sources

description:
FlightPowers cross-source comparison: prices one stay on every source the caller has a key for. Input: a free-text destination the way a person would write it ("Rome", "Tokyo Shibuya"), check-in and check-out dates, and how many adults. Returns one row per source: the cheapest and the median stay total, how many places were found, the currency and when it was read.

Every row carries the caveats that decide whether one source is cheaper. rating_scale is 10 on Booking and 5 on Airbnb. taxes_included is true on Booking, where excluded taxes are folded into the price, and null on Airbnb, where we have not established the tax treatment of the display total; a null is not a no. A source the caller has no key for is listed in providers_skipped and is not counted anywhere in the comparison.

Rates go stale within minutes: a current comparison comes from a new call, not from an earlier result.

adults.description: Number of adult guests. Defaults to the upstream default when omitted.

checkout_date.description: Departure morning, "YYYY-MM-DD". Must be after checkin_date.

children.description: Number of children sharing the room.

currency.description: ISO currency code for every row, e.g. "usd". Sources are asked for the same currency so the totals are comparable; a row that came back in a different one says so in its own currency field and is not converted.

destination.description: Where to stay, in free text the way a person would write it, e.g. "Rome" or "Tokyo Shibuya". A city, district, landmark or region all work; no internal location ID is needed.

providers.description: Which sources to price, e.g. ["booking", "airbnb"]. Defaults to both. A source the caller has no RapidAPI key for is not called and appears in providers_skipped.

name: compare_hotel_rates

outputSchema.description: One stay priced on every source the caller has a key for, one row per source. Whether one source is cheaper than another depends on `caveats` and each row's `search_status`, `rating_scale` and `currency`: a degraded source has no count and no prices, and a skipped source is counted nowhere.

api_usage.description: With the caller's own key: what this call cost their RapidAPI plan, and what remains on it. On a free signed-in search (`trial` present): the day's free-search counter instead, and no plan figures -- the search ran on FlightPowers' key and nothing is billed to the user. Present on every response that reached the upstream, including a degraded one.

hub_requests_billed.description: How many HTTP requests RapidAPI actually billed. Larger than requests_used_by_this_call when a search failed with a server error and was retried, because the retry is billed too. With the caller's own key this is the figure their RapidAPI plan is charged. Absent on a free search.

note.description: The same figures as one plain sentence.

requests_used_by_this_call.description: How many date/destination combinations were searched -- what the answer COVERS.

caveats.description: Sentences on what makes the sources' totals differ -- rating scales, tax treatment, currencies, a source that did not answer.

currency.description: The currency every source was ASKED for.

needs_api_key.description: True when no usable RapidAPI key arrived with the call, or the upstream rejected the one that did. No search was run and nothing was billed; signup_url and message describe the fix.

nights.description: Nights between the two dates, or null when the dates could not be read as dates.

items.description: What one accommodation source answered. Present for every source that was CALLED, whether or not it answered: a source with search_status 'degraded' carries a reason, a null count and no prices, which is not the same answer as a source that found nothing.

count.description: How many properties from this source carried a price. Null when the source did not answer -- zero would read as 'nothing there', which a failed search does not know.

currency.description: The currency THIS row's totals are in. Rows in different currencies are not comparable and nothing is converted.

detail.description: Plain text explaining this row's outcome, written for a person.

provider.description: Which source this row is about, e.g. 'booking'.

rating_scale.description: What a review score from this source is out of: 10 on Booking, 5 on Airbnb, so two raw scores from different sources are not on the same scale.

retrieved_at.description: When these rows were read, taken from the rows themselves rather than from when this answer was assembled.

search_status.description: 'ok': the source answered with priced results. 'empty': it answered and had nothing for that stay -- a real answer. 'degraded': it was asked and could not answer, so count is null and an empty list from it means nothing.

taxes_included.description: Whether this source's totals include tax. Null means it has not been established for that source, not that tax is excluded.

top.description: The cheapest few priced rows from this source.

providers_skipped.description: Sources that were NOT called, each named with why and where to subscribe. A source here contributed nothing to results and is counted nowhere. It is listed rather than dropped because a silently missing source is indistinguishable from a source that had nothing.

reason.description: 'no_key': no RapidAPI key for that source's listing arrived with the call. 'not_subscribed': the key supplied is not subscribed to that listing. 'key_rejected': the key was refused outright.

quota_exhausted.description: True when the caller's RapidAPI plan has no requests left for the current period.

signup_url.description: Where the caller subscribes or changes plan.

outputSchema.title: Cross-source hotel rate comparison

title: FlightPowers: compare hotel rates across sources
